topic: Fastest animal: peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus) — hunting stoop recorded at 389 km/h (242 mph) by falconer Ken Franklin's bird 'Frightful' diving alongside a skydiver over Washington State (National Geographic, 1999–2005); cheetah ~112 km/h (fastest land animal); peregrine populations crashed from DDT in the 1950s–60s, removed from the US endangered species list in 1999, now nesting on skyscrapers and bridges in cities worldwide
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The cheetah is the fastest animal on Earth.
myths.reality: The cheetah is the fastest land animal (~112 km/h); the peregrine falcon's hunting dive, recorded at 389 km/h, is more than three times faster and is the fastest speed of any animal.
